claims.statement: Poland maintains an official register of energy cooperatives and publishes operating guidance, providing a visible and growing target list rather than an undefined market.

Polish regulation specifies registration, balancing, access to metering data, and settlement calculations for energy cooperatives, making auditable allocation logic a recurring operational requirement.

Hypothesis: formation advisers and ESCOs will resell a standard ledger because they currently bear post-launch support costs and need every newly formed cooperative to remain administratively functional.

contrary_evidence: The official register still represents a small domestic customer count, so Poland alone may not support a large outcome.

Electricity sellers and distribution operators already perform parts of statutory settlement, limiting the product to reconciliation, transparency, and administration rather than replacing regulated billing.

economics.acquisition_route: Win advisers that launch multiple cooperatives and bundle the ledger into their administration contract
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: Poland plus two adjacent EU regimes could produce 4 million PLN ARR from roughly 120 cooperatives or platform partners by years 6-8; at 25% EBITDA, a 6-8x EBITDA valuation and 75% founder ownership implies 4.5-6 million PLN of founder equity, making geographic expansion essential
economics.founder_time: 18-24 hours weekly through the first two live settlements, falling toward 10 hours weekly after automated imports and partner-led onboarding
economics.gross_margin_basis: Automated ingestion and ledger calculation could support 75-85% gross margin, with implementation and reconciliation support as the main costs
economics.payback: Target under 9 months because each adviser contract can bring several cooperatives; onboarding effort must be templated
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 8-20 PLN per meter per month with a 12000-30000 PLN annual minimum per cooperative and 30000-80000 PLN adviser licence
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monthly settlement, annual reporting, and member history make the system recurring and difficult to replace mid-operation

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A growing library of operator-specific exceptions, tariff logic, and historical meter reconciliations raises accuracy and switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Administrators and members of Polish energy cooperatives, plus advisers and ESCOs managing them
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Resold by cooperative formation advisers, municipal-energy consultants, ESCOs, and electricity sellers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Multi-tenant settlement and administration SaaS priced per meter, with setup and adviser white-label licences
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The cooperative or its managing adviser pays monthly per metering point when member statements and reconciliation close
fingerprint.problem_trigger: New meter data and supplier statements must be allocated, reconciled, explained, and preserved for each billing period

founder_fit: Strong energy-domain adjacency and quantitative fit, with a credible first network through the family renewable business. Recurring calculations and exception handling suit the founder better than repeated consumer sales, but energy-law review must be delegated.
risks: A narrow Polish market could cap revenue before the founder target is reachable.
Settlement errors can affect many members and require professional liability controls.
Slow municipal procurement could delay adoption despite channel interest.

structure.control_point: The canonical allocation and reconciliation record used to close each cooperative billing cycle
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable, authorised access to meter and supplier data plus defensible interpretation of settlement rules

thesis: Create a meter-allocation, invoice-reconciliation, and member-statement ledger for Polish energy cooperatives, distributed through cooperative formation advisers, municipalities, ESCOs, and obligated electricity sellers. The recurring settlement is the product's anchor; scenario planning and member portals are secondary modules.
title: Co-op Settlement OS
uncertainties: The number of cooperatives that outsource administration and their annual software budget are unknown.
Data formats and cooperation quality differ across sellers and distribution operators.
Expansion to adjacent collective-self-consumption regimes may require country-specific legal logic.
